conflict_resolutions.PARTIAL_OR_QUALIFIED_CHANGE_REQUIRES_CLA: Checked clause by clause against the held Federal Register texts. EO 11609 Sec. 11(5) supersedes only "Section 3 of Executive Order No. 11294" (the delegation to the Bureau of the Budget, an amendment of EO 11230), effective immediately under EO 11609 Sec. 12 because Sec. 11 is not among the paragraphs of section 1 that wait ninety days; it leaves Sections 1, 2 and 4 untouched. Sections 1, 3 and 4 are self-executing amendments or a supersession of EO 10970 and were spent on issue. The Sec. 2 delegation to the Secretary of State continued until EO 12561 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11294 as a whole on July 1, 1986, in the same order that re-delegated the successor authority to the Secretary of State (EO 12561 Sec. 2) and revoked the inserted paragraph (o) of EO 10621 (EO 12561 Sec. 1). EO 12396 (1982) revoked subsections (g), (h), (j), (k), (l), (m) and (n) of Section 1 of EO 10621, not the paragraph (o) that Section 1 of this order added. No held text shows an end of Sec. 2 earlier than 1986-07-01.

rationale: EO 11294 (Delegating certain authority of the President to establish maximum per diem rates for Government civilian personnel in travel status, signed August 4, 1966, 31 FR 10601) has four sections. Sections 1, 3 and 4 amend EO 10621, amend EO 11230 and supersede EO 10970; they were completed on issue. Section 2 delegates to the Secretary of State the President's per diem authority for areas outside the United States, a continuing delegation. EO 12561 Sec. 3, in the held Federal Register text, reads "Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4,1966, is revoked." That instrument, signed July 1, 1986 with no later effective-date wording, also re-delegates the successor authority to the Secretary of State (Sec. 2) and revokes the paragraph (o) that Section 1 of this order added to EO 10621 (Sec. 1), so it ends the Sec. 2 delegation for a stated reason and is not a cleanup of a spent order. The Code note at 3 U.S.C. 301 records that EO 11294 "was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12561, July 1, 1986". The only partial earlier change is EO 11609 Sec. 11(5), superseding Section 3 on July 22, 1971. The history observations (Federal Register disposition notes naming EO 11609 and EO 12561 and the 1989 "revoked" entry) agree. The one CURRENT lead is a 3 U.S.C. 301 note listing EO 10621 as amended by EO 11294; it shows only the consequence in the parent and cannot establish force. Status: no.
